links.outcome: Reading grade level of original versus LLM-simplified patient leaflets versus recommended grade 6
links.effect: LLM-modified PILs mean reading grade 9.5±0.5 vs original 11.1±0.1 (p<0.01); recommended grade 6 not achieved.
links.quote: However, the recommended reading grade of 6 (expected to be understood by 11- to 12-year-old children) was not achieved.

links.outcome: Readability of LLM-generated plain-language patient materials
links.effect: LLM-simplified leaflets reduced reading grade to 9.5±0.5 from 11.1±0.1 but remained above the recommended grade 6.
links.quote: However, the recommended reading grade of 6 (expected to be understood by 11- to 12-year-old children) was not achieved.

links.outcome: Factual accuracy of LLM-modified leaflets as rated by consultant radiologists
links.effect: Most LLM-modified PILs had minor factual accuracy concerns identified by three consultant radiologists; no errors that could cause serious patient harm detected.
links.quote: Human evaluation revealed that most LLM-modified PILs had minor concerns regarding factual accuracy, but no errors that could result in serious patient harm were detected.

screen.reason: Evaluates GPT-4's ability to rewrite interventional radiology patient information leaflets for improved readability and factual accuracy, but does not test or compare an organizational guardrail or deployment practice.
